label: callChat
after:
The rite had ended an hour ago and no one had left.

I counted the offerings still laid along the stone lip — nine, when there should have been eight. Someone had added one after the closing. I did not know whose it was.

Julian stood near the gate. He watched the clearing without speaking. The silver lines on his arms moved once, and he covered them with his sleeve.

A woman in grey crossed to the offering stone, looked at the ninth bowl, and did not touch it. She left by the north path. Two of the assembly watched her go and then looked at me.

I put my hand flat on the stone. It was still warm on one side.

Behind me, the youth was explaining something to her mother in a low voice, the same three words repeating. I could not hear which words.

Julian moved a step closer to the gate and stopped.

after: The rite had ended an hour ago and no one had left. A woman in grey strode straight to the offering stone, lifted the ninth bowl, and held it out toward the assembly. "Whose is this?" she called, her voice sharp enough to stop every conversation. My breath caught as heads turned, two of them fixing on me while the stone's lingering heat still burned against my palm. I crossed the clearing in three steps, took the bowl from her hands, and set it back on the lip where it belonged. Julian stood near the gate; his name alone pulled my gaze for one heartbeat before I forced it away. The silver lines on his arms flared once beneath his sleeve as he watched. The woman in grey did not leave. She planted herself on the north path and waited. Behind me the youth kept repeating the same three words to her mother, louder now, until the sound scraped along my spine. I turned to face the two who still stared and raised my voice. "If you have something to say, say it here." Julian moved one step into the clearing. My hand closed around the tarot deck and I drew the first card without looking, letting it land face-up on the warm stone between us.
